step_by_step_reasoning: 1) An upstream account aggregation service (not drawn) publishes an 'account updated' event with an account ID on the first Kinesis stream. 2) Kinesis triggers a lean, fast Lambda. 3) That Lambda runs a SQL query against RDS (transactional data written by the other service) and receives the user's transactions. 4) It batches them (~100) and publishes transaction description strings to SQS. 5) SQS fans out to many instances of a second Lambda hosting the ANTLR-based NLP parser. 6) The NLP Lambda writes extracted fields plus model version to a second RDS table. 7) The NLP Lambda publishes a completion event to a second Kinesis stream for other teams to consume. The two Kinesis, two Lambda and two RDS icons perform distinct roles so they are kept separate. Jenkins/CloudFormation are deployment-only and omitted. The upstream aggregation service and downstream consumers are not drawn as components and are omitted.

graph.name: Tandem: Transaction Enrichment Data Pipeline with NLP on Lambda
graph.categories: Data Pipeline, Serverless, Machine Learning, NLP, FinTech
graph.notes: Tandem bank aggregates transaction data from UK banks. An event-driven serverless pipeline (Kinesis -> Lambda -> SQS -> Lambda fan-out) extracts merchant name, currency, exchange rate, location and dates from raw transaction descriptions using an ANTLR-generated parser, stores the enriched data in RDS with the model version, and publishes a completion event to Kinesis. SQS was introduced because a single Lambda per Kinesis shard processing sequentially could not keep up with tens of millions of transactions.

nodes.name: Kinesis - Account Updated Event Stream
nodes.notes: Receives an event containing an account ID, published by an upstream account aggregation service once a user's account has been updated (triggered on schedule or when the user logs in/refreshes the app).

nodes.name: Lambda - Transaction Reader / Batcher
nodes.notes: Purposely lean and fast. Listens for the Kinesis event, runs a SQL query against RDS for the user's transactions, groups them into batches of about 100 and publishes the transaction description strings to SQS.

nodes.name: RDS - Transactional Data
nodes.notes: Stores raw transactional data (date, description, amount) written by the upstream account aggregation service.

nodes.name: SQS - Transaction Batch Queue
nodes.notes: Holds messages containing batches of raw transaction description strings. Enables fan-out to many Lambdas, overcoming the one-Lambda-per-Kinesis-shard sequential processing limit.

nodes.name: Lambda - NLP Extraction
nodes.notes: Hosts the NLP model: ANTLR parser generated from a domain-specific grammar, compiled to Python and bundled into the Lambda. Extracts merchant name, currency, exchange rates, merchant location, dates. Processing takes a few seconds; many instances scale out to handle tens of millions of transactions. Originally connected directly to Kinesis. Deployed via Jenkins and CloudFormation using a custom open source bundling tool.

nodes.name: RDS - Extracted Data
nodes.notes: Table with columns for all extracted fields. Stores processed transactions along with the version of the model used, enabling later analysis, comparison and model iteration.

nodes.name: Kinesis - Processing Completed Event Stream
nodes.notes: Event stream signalling that the customer's transactions have finished processing. Other parts of the organization trigger from this event, e.g. refreshing the app with friendly descriptions.

edges.notes: Account-updated event (account ID) on the Kinesis stream triggers the Lambda.
Lambda issues a SQL query to RDS for the transactions of the given user.
RDS returns the user's transactions to the Lambda.
Lambda publishes messages with batches of about 100 transaction description strings to SQS.
SQS messages trigger a fan-out of NLP Lambda invocations, delivering the transaction batches.
Writes the extracted/enriched transaction fields along with the model version to RDS.
Publishes an event indicating that the customer's transactions have finished processing, for downstream consumers.
